name: Kapre
description: The Kapre is a giant, dark-skinned, tobacco-smoking tree-dwelling spirit of Philippine folklore, traditionally associated with large balete, acacia, and mango trees. Generally non-hostile but mischievous and territorial, the kapre is regarded as a guardian of its tree.

aliases.name: Kapre
aliases.language: Tagalog (loanword from Spanish cafre / Arabic kāfir)
aliases.meaning: From Spanish cafre, ultimately Arabic kāfir ('non-believer'); colonial-era pejorative reapplied to a folkloric giant

aliases.name: Agta
aliases.meaning: 'Black one' / dark-skinned forest giant; regional analogue of the kapre

aliases.name: Chapri
aliases.meaning: Earliest Spanish-language attestation, recorded by Antonio Pigafetta during the Magellan expedition

origin: Found throughout the Philippine archipelago, especially in lowland forests, rural barangays, and old agricultural land where balete and other large trees survive.
